svg.title: Fig. 189 — The reciprocal spiral rθ = a with its asymptote at distance a from the initial line
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 189, page 211. Section: spirals.

g.data-text: The pole O, the initial line, and the asymptote: the line parallel to the initial line at the distance a (the limit of r·sin θ as θ → 0 is a).
Take an angle θ and draw the ray OP at that angle from the initial line.
On the ray lay off r = a/θ (θ in radians). Then the arc of the circle about O from the initial line to P has the length r·θ = a, the same for every point of the curve.
Draw the circle about O through P, from the initial line to P: this arc has the length a.
Repeat for other angles and join the points: the branch for θ > 0 comes from the right along the asymptote, crosses OY at (0, 2a/π), passes (−a/π, 0) and winds into O.
The branch for θ < 0 is the mirror image in the axis OY: it comes from the left along the asymptote, crosses at the same point on OY and winds into O the other way.
The book marks the points where the branches meet the axes.
